run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T00:49:30Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert on otel-demo/frontend is backed by the frontend's own error spans: at 2026-11-18T00:49:30Z frontend was recording 0.337 error spans/s (STATUS_CODE_ERROR) versus 44.87/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and its per-operation error series are zero before 00:48 and non-zero from the 00:50:00 sample, so the degradation began in the 00:48-00:50 interval, immediately after the ad and payment Deployments were re-rolled (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:47:56Z on both pod templates; old pods killed 00:47:59/00:48:00, new pods started 00:47:58/00:47:59). The failing frontend operations are /api/data (grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds) and /api/checkout (grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder); the trace error text is transport-level: GetAds fails with '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080' and checkout's Charge fails with 'connect: connection refused' to 100.70.188.60:8080 - those two addresses are the ClusterIPs of Service ad and Service payment, so callers were refused before reaching those services (their own server spans and logs show successful request handling). The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds two fault settings that are switched on and that name exactly these two services - 'adFailure' defaultVariant 'on' ('Fail ad service') and 'paymentFailure' defaultVariant '100%' ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') - and no other object is seen applying a change to ad or payment; as a hypothesis this ConfigMap is the origin of the fault, with the 00:47:56 rollouts as its mechanism and the caller-side connection refusals plus frontend 500s as consequences. That hypothesis is not confirmed: the observed errors are connection-level rather than flag-generated application errors, and neither ad nor payment recorded an ERROR span or an error log line, so the declared faults were not directly observed; times of the flag change are unknown, and endpoint/readiness history is not observable. frontend-proxy and checkout also show their own error spans, while cart, currency, product-catalog, quote, shipping, ad (as a server) and payment (as a server) showed no failing operations in the sampled data.

claims.text: At 2026-11-18T00:49:30Z the frontend service had 0.337037037037037 error spans/s (status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR) against 44.86666666666667 spans/s with STATUS_CODE_UNSET in the same 5m rate window, so the alert signal corresponds to real frontend error spans.

frontend error rates per operation were exactly 0 at the 00:48:00 sample and non-zero from the 00:50:00 sample (GET 0.304, GET /api/data 0.304, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 0.304, POST /api/checkout 0.148, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.148, tcp.connect 0.041), peaked at 1.070/s for GET /api/data and AdService/GetAds at 00:54:00, were still non-zero at the 01:00:00 sample and 0 at the last sample 01:02:00, so the error window began between 00:48 and 00:50.

In traces sampled at 00:48:54-00:49:04, frontend spans 'GET' / 'GET /api/data' and 'POST' / 'POST /api/checkout' carry error=true with http.status_code 500, and the child client spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code 14 for grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds with exception message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080' and rpc.grpc.status_code 13 for grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with message '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"'.

The refused addresses are the Service ClusterIPs: Service ad in otel-demo is 100.65.180.246 with port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, and Service payment is 100.70.188.60 with port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, so both callers were refused at the ad and payment Services, not at a pod IP.

Deployments ad and payment both carry pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:47:56Z together with env AD_PORT=8080 (ad) and PAYMENT_PORT=8080 (payment) and FLAGD_HOST=flagd/FLAGD_PORT=8013; their container images are ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and :2.1.3-payment.

Of the 21 otel-demo Deployments, only ad and payment have restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:47:56Z; flagd has 2026-11-18T00:15:53Z and every other Deployment (including frontend, checkout, frontend-proxy) has no restartedAt annotation, so the 00:47:56 rollout was scoped to ad and payment.

Events in otel-demo record Deployment ad 'Scaled up replica set ad-6cb57f76d from 0 to 1' and 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0', new pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 Scheduled/Created/Started 00:47:56-00:47:58 and old pod ad-554b849958-mbnxm Killing at 00:47:59, and an identical sequence for payment (new pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 started 00:47:59, old pod payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb killed 00:48:00).

Pods ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 are Running with restartCount 0, all pod conditions True (Ready, ContainersReady), and the deployments report 1/1 ready and available replicas; neither pod defines readiness, liveness or startup probes, and their CPU limits are 50m (ad) and 20m (payment).

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds demo.flagd.json with fault settings 'adFailure' defaultVariant 'on' (description 'Fail ad service') and 'paymentFailure' defaultVariant '100%' (description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%'), while adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure are all 'off' in the same document.

ad kept serving: its server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds ran at 0.6122807017543859/s at 00:52:00 and 0.24561403508771928/s at 00:56:00, all with status STATUS_CODE_UNSET and with no ERROR series, and its pod log for 00:48-00:57 contains only 'Targeted ad request received for [...]' / 'Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.' and 'no baggage found in context' lines with no error line (276 lines read, 0 matched an error filter).

payment kept serving too: its server spans 'charge' and 'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' ran at 0.5669707368421052/s at 00:52:00 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no ERROR series, while checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge showed STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.065428/s; payment's pod log for 00:45-01:05 contains 296 matching lines that are all 'Charge request received.' with no error/failure line.

The failure propagated to frontend's callers: in the 30m rate at 00:49:30 the frontend-proxy spans 'ingress' (0.018746739164696612/s) and 'router frontend egress' (0.01249782610979774/s) carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and checkout's own spans oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.005112747044917258/s.

At 00:56:00 frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds was failing at 0.6684210526315789/s with STATUS_CODE_ERROR against 0.24736842105263154/s with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, i.e. most but not all GetAds calls failed at that instant.

Endpoints for Service ad and Service payment currently resolve to the new pods (ad -> ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 100.96.4.142:8080, payment -> payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 100.96.4.221:8080), so the Services' selectors do match the post-rollout pods; this is the state at query time, not during the incident.

Primary candidate cause: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds the enabled fault settings adFailure='on' and paymentFailure='100%', whose names and descriptions target exactly the two services that were re-rolled at 2026-11-18T00:47:56Z and whose calls fail (ad via GetAds, payment via Charge); the rollouts are the mechanism by which those services took up the fault and the caller-side connection refusals plus frontend 500s on /api/data and /api/checkout are its consequences.

Alternative candidate: the errors are purely the transient effect of replacing the single ad and payment pods at 00:47:56-00:48:00 (old pod removed, new pod/endpoints not serving new connections yet), which would produce ECONNREFUSED at the ad and payment ClusterIPs without involving the feature flags; the observed error window of roughly 00:48-01:00 is longer than a few-second pod replacement, so this does not fully account for the duration either.

The observed failure text is transport-level ('connect ECONNREFUSED ...:8080', gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE / 13 INTERNAL wrapping it), not an application error that a flag-driven failure would return; ad's GetAds server spans never carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR and neither ad nor payment wrote an error log line, so the declared adFailure/paymentFailure faults were not directly observed taking effect.

Failure shares stay below the values the flags would imply: at 00:52:00 GetAds had 0.32982456140350874/s errors against 0.6175438596491227/s non-error spans, and checkout's Charge had 0.065428/s errors while payment itself handled 0.5669707368421052 charge spans/s, which is not a boolean ad failure on every call nor a 100% payment failure.

Rejected: ad or payment containers crashed, were OOMKilled, evicted or are crash-looping. Both pods are Running with restartCount 0, all conditions True, their Deployments report 1/1 ready, and the only events involving them are the rollout's Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started plus Killing of the old pods - no OOMKilled, Evicted, BackOff or Unhealthy reason appears.

Rejected: the frontend itself was restarted or failed on its own. Deployment frontend has no restartedAt annotation (unlike ad and payment), the frontend pod has restartCount 0, and every failing frontend span carries a downstream error message (ECONNREFUSED to the ad/payment ClusterIPs or checkout's 13 INTERNAL), placing the failure below frontend.

gaps: Change history is not integrated in this Run (change_history is listed as not_integrated), and ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config carries no timestamps, so I could not determine when adFailure was set to 'on' or paymentFailure to '100%', nor what they were before the incident.

The declared faults themselves were not observed: no ad or payment application error span or error log line attributable to adFailure/paymentFailure exists in the sampled evidence; the collected error text is transport-level connection refusal, so I cannot confirm the flags caused the observed calls to fail.

Endpoint/readiness history is unobservable: queries for kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and any kube_* metric series returned nothing in this Prometheus (unknown, not zero), so I cannot tell whether ad and payment had zero ready endpoints between 00:48 and 01:00, which would be the direct mechanism of ECONNREFUSED at their ClusterIPs.

Jaeger retained traces only for approximately 00:48:54-00:49:04 (later searches in 00:57-00:58 returned no traces), so the errors that metrics show continuing until about 01:00 have no trace-level error detail and their exact cause text is unknown.
flagd pod logs returned no lines for 00:40-01:05, so I could not verify when flagd began serving the changed flag values, and I did not observe any flagd-side change event.
No networkpolicy objects were returned for otel-demo and no resourcequota/endpoint history could be checked, so network-level blocking and endpoint churn are unchecked rather than excluded.
next_steps: Check audit/change history or GitOps history for edits to ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (adFailure, paymentFailure) and for the kubectl rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment at 2026-11-18T00:47:56Z to establish intent and timing.

Verify whether reverting adFailure to 'off' and paymentFailure to '0%' (and restarting ad and payment) clears frontend's /api/data and /api/checkout 500s, which would confirm or refute the flag hypothesis.
Inspect the flagd instance/flagd-ui state and evaluation logs during the incident window to confirm the services actually received the enabled flag values.

Add readiness probes to ad and payment so their endpoints are not published before the applications listen on port 8080, and compare frontend error rate against a baseline period when the flags were off.
